caption:
Smart business owners don't just claim more. They time it.

3 moves before 30 June:

1. Bring forward deductions. Pay rent, insurance, subscriptions and other deductible costs before 30 June — up to 12 months ahead (12-month rule for prepayments). Claim it this year.

2. Defer income. If you're on a cash basis, income is assessable when you receive it, not when you earn it. Invoice after 30 June for work completed in June if you can.

3. Top up super before 30 June. Your contribution must be received by the fund before 30 June for it to count this year. Allow 3–5 business days for it to clear.

This is timing. Not avoidance.

Save this for June.

General info only, not personal advice.

figures_checked: Prepayment 12-month rule: deductible expenses paid up to 12 months ahead before 30 June (ATO standard rule for small business)
Super contributions: must be received by fund before 30 June to count in that year (ATO, standard rule)
Cash basis income timing: assessable when received (ATO, standard rule)
